title: Unit Circle Definition
text: $$\cos\left(\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)$$ represents the x-coordinate of the point on the unit circle at the angle $$\frac{7\pi}{6}.$$\n##figure1.gif##

title: Reference Angle
text: The reference angle for $$\frac{7\pi}{6}$$ is $$\frac{\pi}{6}.$$ The absolute values of the coordinates are given by the legs of a $$30-60-90$$ triangle with hypotenuse $$1$$. The $$y-$$ coordinate length is $$\frac{1}{2}.$$ The $$x-$$ coordinate is obtained from the Pythagorean theorem: $$\sqrt{1**2-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)**2}=\sqrt{\frac{3}{4}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.$$\n##figure2.gif##

title: Quadrant Sign
text: The angle $$\frac{7\pi}{6}$$ is in the third quadrant, where $$x-$$ coordinates are negative. Therefore, $$\cos\left(\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)=\frac{-\sqrt{3}}{2}.$$\n##figure3.gif##
